title: Add release tagging and changelog generation
author: Connor O'Brien
release_notes: Adds a repeatable release workflow for redwood-terraform: standardized tags (vX.Y.Z), automated CHANGELOG generation, and a version bump helper for module metadata. No runtime/infra behavior changes.
body: Summary: This PR introduces an opinionated release workflow for redwood-terraform so we can cut alpha module versions consistently (tags + changelog + lightweight automation) without relying on ad-hoc manual steps. This is intended to support the VPC Terraform modules (alpha) program and aligns with the module versioning/release process doc. Motivation: We’ve started landing a steady stream of alpha changes (VPC, endpoints, flow logs, IAM scaffold, CI). Field teams and design partners need pinned versions and readable deltas. Today, we’re manually tagging and writing release notes, and the process is already diverging between maintainers. Goals: (1) One button / one command path to cut a release; (2) deterministic tags (vX.Y.Z); (3) generated CHANGELOG entries based on merged PR metadata; (4) minimal GitHub token scope; (5) guardrails to avoid releasing from dirty or non-main states. Non-goals: publishing to Terraform Registry (external) in alpha; changing module source layout; enforcing conventional commits across all contributors (we’ll encourage, not block). What’s included: - GitHub Actions release workflow: .github/workflows/release.yml supports workflow_dispatch with inputs (version, prerelease flag). It validates we’re on main at a clean commit, creates an annotated tag vX.Y.Z, generates/update CHANGELOG.md, and creates a GitHub Release with the same notes. - Changelog tooling: adds .cliff.toml (git-cliff config) and a scripts/release/generate_changelog.sh wrapper. We generate a scoped section for the version being released and keep CHANGELOG.md append-only. - Version bump automation: scripts/release/bump_version.sh updates module version references where we currently duplicate them (README snippet blocks + examples/* pinned module refs). This keeps examples aligned with the latest release tag. - PR labeling conventions: introduces a lightweight convention to improve changelog quality without blocking merges: labels release-note:feature|fix|security|ops|breaking (breaking allowed but requires explicit acknowledgement). The release script will still work without labels, but output will be less structured. - Safety checks: workflow refuses to run if the repo has uncommitted changes (for local scripts), if version doesn’t match semver, or if the tag already exists. Also enforces the v prefix. - Docs: adds RELEASE.md with step-by-step instructions and a "release dry run" command path for maintainers. Changed areas (high level): - .github/workflows/release.yml (new) - .github/workflows/changelog-check.yml (new; verifies CHANGELOG.md format + that it’s updated when release-note labels are present) - scripts/release/bump_version.sh (new) - scripts/release/generate_changelog.sh (new) - .cliff.toml (new) - CHANGELOG.md (seed file w/ initial alpha notes) - RELEASE.md (new) - Makefile (adds release-dry-run and changelog targets) Notes on permissions/security: The release workflow uses GitHub Actions built-in token with explicit permissions (contents: write). No PATs. The workflow does not assume access to customer accounts or infra. It only tags/releases this repo. It runs only via workflow_dispatch and is restricted to maintainers via repo settings (documented in RELEASE.md). Test plan: - Local: make changelog (verifies git-cliff runs and produces expected output); make release-dry-run (runs semver validation + changelog generation without pushing tags). - CI: ran on this PR: lint + fmt + validate + checkov + tflint all green; workflow yamllint pass. Release workflow itself validated via act-style dry run (documented) and by running workflow on a test tag in a fork. Rollout: once merged, maintainers can cut v0.1.0-alpha.1 (or v0.1.0) following RELEASE.md. We’ll use this for the next design partner drop and update the alpha release notes doc accordingly. Follow-ups: - After we land a few releases, revisit whether we want to enforce release-note labels as a required check. - Consider adding provenance / attestations (SLSA) once we start distributing beyond design partners.
commits: chore(release): add release workflow and tagging guardrails
chore(changelog): add git-cliff config + generation script
chore(versioning): add bump_version helper and update examples
docs: add RELEASE.md and maintainer checklist
ci_summary: CI: pass. Checks: terraform fmt/validate (pass), tflint (pass), checkov (pass), unit smoke scripts (pass), workflow lint (pass). One transient checkov flake on first run due to rate limiting; rerun succeeded.
review_conversation: Irene Choi (Infra) 2025-07-09: This is the right direction. Two requests before approval: (1) make sure workflow has minimal token permissions (explicitly set permissions block), and (2) add a hard guard that releases only run from main (no releasing from a random SHA/branch). Connor O'Brien 2025-07-09: Ack on both. I’ll add permissions: { contents: write } and assert github.ref == refs/heads/main. Also adding a confirmation prompt via workflow input. Sahana Iyer 2025-07-10: Please avoid introducing another toolchain dependency that’s hard to run on CI runners. Does git-cliff require extra install? Also suggest adding a make target and pinning a version. Connor O'Brien 2025-07-10: Added a pinned git-cliff action version for CI and documented local install options; make changelog now uses the containerized runner when available. Devon Price 2025-07-11: Release.yml should not write back to the repo unless the run is explicitly marked "cut release". In the current version it commits CHANGELOG.md automatically; I’d prefer the workflow creates a release from generated notes without pushing a commit, OR pushes only if approved. Connor O'Brien 2025-07-11: Updated: workflow now generates notes for the GitHub Release and (optionally) opens a PR to update CHANGELOG.md instead of committing directly to main. For alpha we default to "open PR" mode. Marcus Lin (Security) 2025-07-12: Thanks for removing PAT usage. Please confirm the workflow does not use third-party actions with broad permissions. Also add a note that release workflow is maintainer-only and should be protected by environment approvals. Connor O'Brien 2025-07-12: Confirmed. We’re using official actions + git-cliff action pinned to a SHA. Added GitHub Environment requirement to RELEASE.md; also scoped permissions and added concurrency to avoid parallel tag creation. Irene Choi 2025-07-15: Approving. The environment gating + main-only check addresses my concerns. Please coordinate first real release with me so we can sanity check tag naming (v0.x.y) aligns with the alpha versioning standard. Connor O'Brien 2025-07-15: Will do; I’ll schedule a 15-min release runthrough before cutting v0.1.0-alpha.1.
merge_outcome: Merged via squash into main by Connor O'Brien after approvals from Infra, CI, and Security reviewers.
